const d=document.getElementById('sideDocs');if(!d)return; d.innerHTML=`

NES Forge ${R.version} — ${R.name}

A standalone visual NES editor, assembler, ROM builder and experimental emulator. Alpha · Roadmap Workbench candidate. Work through the existing tabs. Examples are ordinary editable project files included in the release package.

Ninja Gaiden and Zelda II investigation

RE / DISASM → Open spatial RE workbench now includes connected native scene art, object records, actor parameter/dispatch tables, CHR banks, source labels, RAM leads and coverage gaps for the two investigated revisions. Ninja Gaiden includes shared player/enemy/projectile scripts and poses. Zelda II includes native side-view construction and Link pose/facing output; animation timing and full collision/AI remain unresolved. Inspection stays detached and exports source-scoped evidence. Prepare editable assets previews a self-contained bundle with original initial-art pixels and palettes, paged scene layouts, shared metatile libraries, editable room worlds, selected poses and recovered Ninja script update ticks. Import into current project appends these in one Undo step; Download standalone project opens independently. Open editable resource bundle accepts .nfassets.json without the ROM. Open imported World jumps to the new room map; coverage identifies unassigned collision and reference-only native connections. Recover / import audio opens the same RE ROM in the Audio library without replacing the live emulator. Preview a finite supported music or single-channel SFX transcription, then Import into tracker and save the ordinary project to preserve both spatial and audio assets. DPCM, short-mode noise and native gameplay triggers are not transcribed. Spatial bundles do not include the separately imported audio. Untimed Zelda poses stay untimed, and collision, AI, physics and code remain reference evidence. The first imported page joins the build set; additional pages start excluded, and ROM capacity limits still apply. Zelda II visible PPU address reloads now update both scanline rendering and its capture trace.

Native engine edit/build

RE → Open spatial RE workbench → choose Zelda II → Prepare native edit/build project → Import native game as new project. This replaces the workspace with preserved original ROM bytes, an editable location recipe and one reference room World. Build & Run uses the native banked engine. An unedited build is byte-identical; supported X/Y, scene-selector and entry-code edits preserve every other byte and packed flag. Use the native location controls, Undo/Redo and ordinary Save Project As. Native project schema 13 prevents older editors from discarding the recipe. Ordinary projects retain schema 12, existing recipe identities and generated ROM bytes. Edits to reference art or generic runtime settings block the native build until an encoder exists. This bounded milestone does not reconstruct the entire game or provide reusable movement-rule compilation. The source-independent fixed-size packed-record codec is reusable in fresh projects; the Zelda location layout is an engine adapter.

Start, open and recover

A fresh workspace starts with one blank scene. New Project creates a blank fixed room with the existing single-room build settings. Open Project loads a complete JSON or ZIP project. Browser recovery remains available through Restore / Dismiss; it is protected while being checked or awaiting your choice. New Project and Open Forge ROM have undoable replacement boundaries. A normal project open starts a new history.

# Reproducible tests — NES Forge 2.0.0-alpha.4

Run from a clean release extraction with Node.js 20+ and Python 3:

```sh
python3 tools/bundle.py --check
node tests/run_all.cjs
```

The strict runner tests `mainline/NES_Forge_2.0.0-alpha.4.html`, requires all 44 suites, writes fresh per-suite reports/logs and verifies that the candidate and every provenance input remain unchanged. Missing inputs, skips, filters, source injection or older-HTML fallback fail the gate.

## Retained coverage

The 17 original behavioral suites retain editor/history, codecs, metasprites, animation/entity editing, collision, single-room generation and bundled-emulator gameplay. Six architecture suites retain ProjectStore/lifecycle, whole-ROM goldens, service routing, recognized-format rejection and source convergence. The 47-case World suite retains its behavior with intentional schema-12 expectations. Audio remains a 17-case suite. Gameplay Core adds 35 explicit cases.

The five complete-ROM oracles under `fixtures/golden167/` are immutable. Builds with Gameplay Core unused must remain byte-identical. Frozen 1.6.6, 1.6.7, 1.7 and 1.8 artifacts retain their own 479, 559, 606 and 623 measured totals; those are not 1.9.0 results.

## Audio Runtime / Studio coverage

`audio-runtime180.cjs` covers retained Audio persistence and actual frozen-1.7 rejection; detached tracker/instrument/SFX planning; missing/ambiguous links; unsupported DPCM/effects/custom assembly; generated viewer, single-room and World 6502/APU execution; duty/volume/arpeggio; sound-event timing; SFX preemption/restore; World source round trip; Audio controls; MIDI and MusicXML conversion; preserved SFX indices; undo; and frozen 1.8 example provenance.

`gameplay-core190.cjs` covers the four identity boundaries, generation-safe slot reuse, deterministic state tables, explicit operation/component schemas, executable-profile parity/rejection, exact 64/max+1 persistent capacity, explicit Room/World persistence, cross-owner rejection, unknown-operation preservation/build rejection, complete typed-table authoring, UI-authored Room reconstruction, execution of all five templates, retained-Player binding behavior, linked destination-World actors, unreachable diagnostics, 12/13 whole-plan capacity, disabled-Behavior inertness/re-enable behavior, unsigned overlap boundaries in both generated backends, partial single-room recovery, one-way active-state semantics, legacy ROM parity, the editable example and actual frozen-1.8 schema-12 rejection.

The editable examples can be regenerated before the release gate:

```sh
node tools/build_world_example.cjs
node tools/build_audio_example.cjs
node tools/build_gameplay_example.cjs
```

Examples are hashed runner inputs and must not change during a measured run.

## Evidence limits

The VM harness has a mock DOM and controlled storage/timers. Bundled-emulator execution validates generated instructions and APU state under that emulator. It does not establish real-browser layout, native picker behavior, audible speaker output or independent NES hardware timing. See `../docs/BROWSER_QA.md`.

Current clean-extraction evidence belongs under `../checkpoints/mobile-keyboard-1-clean-extraction/`; historical checkpoint names retain their original release meaning.

## Runtime investigation

The full gate retains all 38 analysis/navigation/recovery/mobile/core suites and adds `re-runtime`, `re-runtime-ui` and `re-runtime-integration`. Actual totals come from the frozen candidate report. The owner's Pepsi ROM is an exact input fixture, not a production recognition allowlist; Bridge Room supplies a sound-producing comparison. Keep model/VM/bundled-emulator evidence separate from browser/manual checks in `../docs/RE_RUNTIME_CHECKLIST.txt`.

## Retained Mobile Playback correction

The gate retains all 921 explicit cases across the 42 Audio Correction suites and adds `mobile-playback200.cjs`. New totals are measured from fresh case records; this document does not predict a pass count. The packager preserves each old suite count, the 26 Audio Correction cases, and every earlier regression floor.

`source-preservation200.cjs` reverses only the exact declared five-file Mobile Playback delta to the frozen `audio-correction-1` candidate, then reverses the original four-file Audio Correction delta to the frozen `re-runtime-1` candidate. The source module order and every restored byte must match their pinned reference hashes. Historical fixtures, whole-ROM oracles, and previous source-delta records remain unchanged.

Frame pacing, capture representation, touch/focus isolation, and timing diagnostics are tested independently of phone acceptance. Three fresh browser reports remain mandatory; an unavailable browser must record a blocked run with zero checks, not a pass. The owner's Cricket Dream 5G / Chrome test is separate from VM and desktop evidence.

## Mobile Keyboard correction

The current gate retains all 940 explicit cases across the 43 Mobile Playback suites and adds the 24 cases in `mobile-keyboard200.cjs` (964 required cases across 44 suites). The packager pins all retained suite counts, including the 26 Audio Correction cases and 19 Mobile Playback cases. New totals come from fresh case records.

The source-preservation chain first reverses only the exact three-file Mobile Keyboard UI/release delta to the frozen `mobile-playback-1` candidate, before applying the two older exact deltas described above. `tools/generate_mobile_keyboard_delta.py` reproduces this reviewable delta from the pinned alpha.2 HTML and source byte boundaries; no historical oracle is regenerated. The original regression suite executes the complete chain and checks the actual candidate bundle against these sources before inspecting protected source blocks.

Direct native tracker keyboard events, composition, canonical undo/persistence, desktop parity, and input isolation have focused VM coverage. These reports do not establish Android keyboard appearance, keyboard layout, touchscreen interaction, speaker output, or physical controller acceptance. Fresh browser reports and owner device review remain separate evidence.

The owner withdrew alpha.3's separate Audio forms. Its 18 form-specific cases are explicitly superseded by the direct keyboard suite; its source and measured reports remain historical evidence, not active acceptance requirements. The candidate starts from alpha.2 and retains all of its 940 cases.

# Reproducible tests — current candidate

Run from `app/` with Node 20+ and Python 3:

```sh
python3 tools/bundle.py --check
FORGE_TEST_WORKERS=2 node tests/run_all.cjs
```

The standard gate retains 116 predecessor suites and 2,046 cases, then runs the declared context-cleanup suites. It requires fresh case records and unchanged inputs, and keeps browser/manual results separate. See [the current test policy](../TEST_POLICY.md) and [historical coverage notes](../docs/history/context-cleanup-1/Tests_README.md).
